deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page belongs to Gauss's Hanoverian triangulation in the Bremen–Zeven–Lüneburg Heath region. It works in Gauss's plane conformal coordinates, in metres. x is measured toward the south and is negative north of Göttingen; y is measured toward the west. Plane azimuths are counted from south through west, so Δx = s·cos(α) and Δy = s·sin(α). The page has three parts: (A) secondary points ('Nebenpunkte') fixed by intersection; (B) a re-adjusted table for the main points Bremen, Brelit, Garlste and Zeven, after an error noted earlier (the 'Fehler' corrects Garlste's coordinates from the previous page); (C) many more secondary points.

COLUMN STRUCTURE (all entries). Each entry has the form: station, observed direction, reduction δ, and residual (computed minus reduced observed). The reduction converts the observed (geodesic) direction into the direction of the straight chord in the projection plane. Numerically, every reduction I tested fits δ ≈ −ρ·(x2−x1)(2y1+y2)/(6R²), with ρ = 206265" and R ≈ 6.3845e6 m [my identification].
- This is the standard Gauss/Gauss–Krüger arc-to-chord correction, written with the axes of this system.
- Examples: Bremen→Garlste gives +4.113 (written +4.115); Bremen→Bottel gives −0.816 (−0.816); Brelit→Bremen gives −6.298 (−6.302); Zeven→Steinberg gives −3.748 (−3.750).
- Further examples: Litberg→Tostedt gives −0.581 (−0.580); Bullerberg→Rotenburg gives −0.522 (−0.522); Falkenberg→Asendorf gives −0.492 (−0.493).

A. TOSTEDT (x=−195286.785, y=15609.854). The listed directions are azimuths observed AT Wilsede, Bullerberg and Litberg TOWARD Tostedt; this is forward intersection.
- Check, Wilsede→Tostedt: Δx = −12907.529 and Δy = +15399.518, so α = 180° − arctan(1.193064) = 129°58'8" (matches).
- Wilsede and Bullerberg have residual 0, i.e. the point was intersected from those two rays alone.
- Litberg: the computed azimuth is 331°30'5.9" [mine]. The reduced observation is 331°30'2.0" − 0.580" = 1.42". The residual is therefore +4.47" (written +4.480).

VERDEN JOHANNIS. It is likewise intersected from Steinberg and Bremen, so no residuals are given. Checks: Steinberg gives α = arctan(3196.291/8241.664) = 21.198° (matches). Bremen gives α = 302.09°, with reductions −0.958 and −3.001 (written −0.959 and −3.003).

B. RE-ADJUSTED TABLEAU. Text: 'Since the error noted above has only very slight influence on the azimuths at the preceding points, the table has here been corrected only with respect to the last points, where it then stands thus.' For each station there are four columns: observed direction (after orientation), reduction, reduced direction, residual.
- All additions check, e.g. 49.430 + 4.115 = 53.545.
- Each residual equals the adjusted plane azimuth minus the reduced direction. Lines already on the previous page keep their old adjusted values, with the back azimuth equal to α ± 180° exactly, as it must be in a plane.
- Bremen: the residuals −0.183, −0.586, +0.646, +0.111, −0.818, +0.832 sum to +0.002.
- Brelit: +0.586 + 0.183 − 0.769 = 0.
- Garlste: −0.183 + 0.183 = 0.
- Zeven: the residuals sum to about 0.002 when Brüttendorf, written in parentheses, is excluded. Its value (+0.654) = 197°21'48.445" − 180° − 17°21'47.791" is shown only for information.

NEW ADJUSTED LINES. Each is given as azimuth, log s, Δx, Δy:
- Zeven–Brelit: 124°13'50.001", 4.3620325, −12947.140, +19029.298.
- Bremen–Brelit: 199°41'51.277", 4.5925671, −36845.154, −13190.717.
- Bremen–Garlste: 165°11'53.362", 4.3325331, −20791.057, +5493.950.
- Brelit–Garlste: 49°19'49.521", 4.3915409, +16054.093, +18684.664.

COMPUTATION OF Δx, Δy. Δx = s·cos α and Δy = s·sin α were computed with logarithms.
- The block of rows gives log s, then log|cos α| (9.7501413, 9.9738133, 9.9853435, 9.8140449), then log|sin α| (9.9173903, 9.5277013, 9.4073516, 9.8799444). I verified all of these.
- Resulting coordinates [mine]: Brelit from Zeven is (−209917.811, 63159.040); Brelit from Bremen is (−209917.809, 63159.049).
- Garlste from Bremen is (−193863.712, 81843.716); Garlste from Brelit is (−193863.717, 81843.709). The closure is at the mm–cm level.
- This replaces the earlier Garlste value of −193863.810 (and y ≈ 81843.684).

TRIANGLE CHECKS. In each triangle the columns are: angle, observed minus adjusted, log sin(angle), log of the opposite side.
- Zeven–Bremen–Brelit: the angles 70°47'43.345", 33°44'15.379" and 75°28'1.276" sum to exactly 180°0'0.000" (plane triangle). Observed minus adjusted is −1.802, −1.232, −1.355 respectively. For example, at Zeven 124°13'49.232" − 53°26'7.689" = 70°47'41.543". The reduced observed angles thus close with −4.389".
- Sine rule for that triangle: log a − log sin A = 4.6174342 for all three angles.
- Bremen–Brelit–Garlste: the angles 34°29'57.915", 29°37'58.244" and 115°52'3.841" sum to exactly 180°. These are differences of the adjusted azimuths. Observed minus adjusted is +0.403, +0.403, −0.366. The sine-rule constant is 4.6384193 for all three.

C. FURTHER SECONDARY POINTS. These follow the same scheme, with directions observed at the main stations toward the new point; parenthesised numbers are evidently weights or numbers of repetitions. Every azimuth I recomputed from the coordinates agrees to the minute.
- Kirchwalsede: Bullerberg 5°19'09" and Wilsede 66°13'32" (residual ≈ +3", written +2.988).
- Asendorf: from Steinberg and from 'Falkenberg' (82°12').
- Schessel: Litberg 20°14'.
- Sittensen: Litberg 30°25.9'.
- Rotenburg: Bullerberg 5°45.7'.
- Brokel: two coordinate versions, the first in red ink. Wilsede 73°51.6'.
- Schneverdingen: Wilsede 61°10.3'; Bullerberg 281°25'.
- Verden Dom: Steinberg 19°42'.
- Achim: Steinberg 96°20'; Bremen 296°55.5'.
- Kirch-Weihe: Steinberg 90°0'09"; Bremen 333°01'.

PURPOSE. The page densifies the Hanover triangulation with church towers and other secondary points, and makes a local least-squares correction of the Bremen/Brelit/Garlste/Zeven figure.
errors: Bullerberg→Kirchwalsede: the reduction is written −1.785". The formula used everywhere else on the page gives about −1.414". With −1.414 the residual is about 0.0", consistent with the listed Corr. −0.031; with −1.785 it would be about +0.38". This is probably a slip, or overwriting/misreading of the figure.

Bullerberg→Tostedt: the reduction is written +0.948", but the formula gives about +0.982". The ratios for Wilsede and Litberg fit the formula to within 0.3%. This may be a small slip, or the reduction was computed with provisional coordinates. The effect is nil here because that ray was used to fix the point (residual 0).
Steinberg→Kirchwalsede: +0.296" against a predicted +0.283". This is a minor discrepancy, possibly from provisional coordinates; the 493 in Kirchwalsede's x is overwritten.

Triangle Zeven–Bremen–Brelit: the reduced observed angles close with −4.389", which is large for Gauss's network. This explains the noticeable residuals at Zeven (−1.033 and +0.769) and at Bremen. It is not an arithmetic error.
Brelit from Zeven and from Bremen differs by 2 mm in x and 9 mm in y. This is ordinary 7-figure log rounding, not an error.
All other additions, subtractions, residuals, log sin/log cos values, sine-rule constants and angle sums that I checked are correct.

results.what: Coordinates of secondary points by forward intersection from directions observed at main stations, with residuals for over-determined rays
results.modern_name: Forward intersection (Vorwärtseinschneiden) in plane grid coordinates
results.usually_credited_to: Standard surveying practice; systematized in Gauss's Hanover survey of the 1820s

results.what: Reduction of observed directions to plane chords via δ ≈ ρ(x2−x1)(2y1+y2)/(6R²), with R ≈ 6.38e6 m
results.modern_name: Arc-to-chord (t−T) correction of the Gauss conformal (Gauss–Krüger type / Hanover) projection

results.what: Local re-adjustment of the Zeven–Bremen–Brelit–Garlste figure, with residuals balancing to zero per station, plane triangle checks (180° and sine rule)

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine working computation from Gauss's Hanover triangulation: intersection of secondary points, the known projection reduction formula, and a small least-squares correction. Gauss's methods here are thoroughly documented (Werke IX, Gaede, Schreiber). It is of interest only as primary data.

The adjusted plane angles of triangle Bremen–Brelit–Garlste sum to exactly 180° (result 0).

transcription_corrections: '[Bu]tlerberg' throughout should read 'Bullerberg' (the station of the previous page's list, y = +35400.171).
At Asendorf, '[Ste]lkenberg (10)' should read 'Falkenberg (10)'. The azimuth of 82°12' and the reduction of −0.493 fit Falkenberg's coordinates (−146619.041, 5142.503).
The connective in the German note is uncertain ('so [ist]' / 'so [habe ich]'). The sense is: 'the table has here been corrected only with respect to the last points'.
At Zeven, the Brüttendorf residual (+0.654) is written in parentheses in the manuscript, marking it as excluded from the orientation.

Several final digits are overwritten in bold in the image: Verden Johannis 276; Kirchwalsede 493; Schessel 415; Asendorf/Steinberg residual 1.776; Garlste log 4.4073516. These look like later corrections, not alternative readings.
The Brokel line in red ink (−174341.737, +27991.082, 'Ba…') and the red third-column residuals (−2.50, −1.73, +0.023, −0.254) are a later revision layer.
The column of coordinates in the left margin (−146619.041, …) is bleed or a facing-page view of the previous page's coordinate list, not content of this folio.
